instructions.content: Ask the confidence-audit question and the blind-spot question sequentially, never both in the same message -- wait for the user's response to each before asking the next.
Generate 3-7 specific confidence items, each naming what was done, what was not verified, and why confidence is low -- not a vague feeling.
For the blind-spot check, target assumptions the user stated but that went unverified, alternatives not explored, and signals dropped mid-conversation.
If a flagged item is a verified, concrete gap not being fixed in this session, create a known-issue document via context-file with an honest severity rating -- do not leave it as only a chat mention.
Before treating the session as closed, confirm with the user that the reflection addressed their concerns and explicitly ask if anything else needs addressing.
NEVER skip the reflection because the session feels complete -- the agent is a poor judge of its own completeness.
NEVER give a vague confidence item such as "not confident about performance" -- name the specific file, function, or assumption.
NEVER ask both reflection questions in one breath -- combining them reduces the thoughtfulness of each answer.
NEVER deflect or make excuses for a low-confidence item -- excuses undermine the honesty the reflection depends on.
NEVER spawn a sub-agent reflection without a concrete session summary -- a vague prompt produces vague output.
NEVER let a verified-but-deferred gap live only as a chat mention -- file it as a known-issue document in the same turn.
Do NOT trigger this skill for brief single-answer queries, CI/automated contexts, or in the middle of active work -- only when a session appears to be concluding.
LOW and MEDIUM severity ratings on a known-issue entry are legitimate, honest outcomes -- do not inflate severity just to make an item feel actioned.
